items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: if f : X -> Y is a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over S, then the underlying map of topological spaces |f| : |X| -> |Y| is quasi-compact, i.e. the preimage of every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact (source lines 1266-1271). The proof realizes a quasi-compact open V of |Y| as the underlying set of an open subspace Y', uses that Y' is then a quasi-compact algebraic space, so that X' = Y' x_Y X is quasi-compact by the definition of quasi-compactness of f, identifies |X'| with |f|^{-1}(V) via the description of the points of the fibre product, and concludes that this preimage is a quasi-compact open of |X|.
